I. GENERAL
Acts of violence against women and children constitute violations of human rights, therefore their dignity and honor need to be protected and their right to life guaranteed in accordance with their nature and disposition without discrimination.

In order to prevent and overcome violence against women and children in Pulang Pisau Regency so that they are protected from violence, threats of violence, torture or treatment that degrades human dignity and honor, it is necessary to provide protection for women and children in the form of regional regulations.

Thus far, laws and regulations governing the protection of women and children from acts of violence have not yet regulated protection efforts at the Regional level, therefore institutional support and regulations are needed that can guarantee its implementation.

The Regional Regulation regulates protection efforts for women and children, particularly in terms of prevention, services and empowerment of women and children from acts of violence in Pulang Pisau Regency.

Article 8
(1) The obligations and responsibilities of the community as referred to in Article 6 letter b shall be implemented in the form of community participation. (2) The forms of community participation as referred to in paragraph (1), include:
a. preventing the occurrence of acts of violence in various forms, exploitation, discrimination, mistreatment and/or treatment that degrades the degree and dignity of humanity towards women and children;
b. providing information and/or reporting acts of violence in various forms, exploitation, discrimination, mistreatment and/or treatment that degrades the degree and dignity of humanity towards women and children to law enforcement or the authorized parties; and
c. participating in providing assistance and/or handling of victims of acts of violence in various forms, exploitation, discrimination, mistreatment and/or treatment that degrades the degree and dignity of humanity towards women and children.
(3) Forms of participation shall be implemented responsibly in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

CHAPTER XII
SANCTION PROVISIONS
Article 26
(1) Every person who intentionally fails to provide protection to women and children thereby causing violence, allows violence to occur, and/or does not report and does not provide protection to victims, shall be subject to sanctions as stipulated in the applicable laws and regulations.
(2) Officials appointed to administer protection who fail to carry out their obligations and responsibilities shall be subject to administrative action or sanctions.
(3) UPTD-PPA managers who carry out service duties, if they violate service principles, may be subject to sanctions in accordance with the internal mechanisms of UPTD-PPA.

NUMBER 6 OF 2024
CONCERNING
THE IMPLEMENTATION OF PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN

I. GENERAL
Acts of violence against women and children constitute violations of human rights, therefore their dignity and honor need to be protected and their right to life guaranteed in accordance with their nature and disposition without discrimination.

In order to prevent and overcome violence against women and children in Pulang Pisau Regency so that they are protected from violence, threats of violence, torture or treatment that degrades human dignity and honor, it is necessary to provide protection for women and children in the form of regional regulations.

Thus far, laws and regulations governing the protection of women and children from acts of violence have not yet regulated protection efforts at the Regional level, therefore institutional support and regulations are needed that can guarantee its implementation.

The Regional Regulation regulates protection efforts for women and children, particularly in terms of prevention, services and empowerment of women and children from acts of violence in Pulang Pisau Regency.

Article 19
The community may conduct supervision of the implementation of PPA regarding protection from acts of violence in various forms, exploitation, discrimination, mistreatment and/or treatment that degrades human dignity, which is carried out by the Regional Government, through a mechanism for conveying aspirations to the Regent or to the DPRD.

Article 24
(1) The Regional Government may provide funding assistance to community organizations, social organizations, or non-governmental organizations that implement PPA against acts of violence in various forms, exploitation, discrimination, mistreatment and/or treatment that degrades the degree and dignity of humanity.
(2) The funding assistance shall be provided in accordance with regional financial capacity and implemented in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations in the field of regional finance.

Article 22
(1) Social community organizations that participate in the implementation of protection for victims as referred to in article 21 paragraph 2, shall be given guidance by the Regional Government.
(2) Guidance may take the form of social guidance, skills guidance and operational technical guidance.

CHAPTER I
GENERAL PROVISIONS
Article 1
In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:
1. Region is Pulang Pisau Regency. 2. Regional Government is the regional head as an element of regional government administration who leads the implementation of government affairs that are the authority of the autonomous region. 3. Regent is the Regent of Pulang Pisau. 4. Regional House of Representatives hereinafter abbreviated as DPRD is a regional people's representative institution that is positioned as an element of regional government administration. 5. Regional Apparatus is an auxiliary element of the Regional head and Regional House of Representatives in the administration of Government Affairs that are the authority of the Region. 6. Child is a person who has not reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including a child still in the womb. 7. Protection of Women and Children hereinafter abbreviated as PPA is a handling effort to protect and fulfill the rights of women and children from all forms of violence, discrimination, special protection, and other problems. 8. Violence is any unlawful act with or without the use of means against physical and psychological integrity that causes danger to life or body or results in the deprivation of a person's freedom. 9. Violence against women is any action based on gender differences that results in or may result in misery or suffering of women physically, sexually or psychologically, economic exploitation, social, including threats of certain actions, coercion or deprivation of freedom arbitrarily, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life. 10. Violence against children is any act against a child that results in misery or suffering physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically, economic exploitation, social, including neglect and maltreatment that threatens bodily integrity and degrades the dignity of the child. 11. Domestic violence is any act against a person especially women that results in misery or suffering physically, sexually, psychologically and or domestic neglect including threats to commit acts of coercion or deprivation of freedom unlawfully within the scope of the household. 12. Physical violence is any act that results in pain, injury, wounds or disability to a person's body, miscarriage, fainting and or causes death. 13. Sexual violence is any act in the form of sexual harassment, forced sexual intercourse, forced sexual intercourse in an unnatural or unwanted manner, forced sexual intercourse with others for commercial purposes and or certain purposes. 14. Economic violence is any act that deliberately neglects family members in the form of not providing a proper living care or maintenance. 15. Psychological violence is any act that results in fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and or severe psychological suffering to a person. 16. Human trafficking is the act of recruitment, transportation, harboring, sending, transfer, or receipt of a person by threat of violence, use of violence, abduction, confinement, forgery, fraud, abuse of power or position of vulnerability, debt bondage or giving payment or benefits, so as to obtain consent from the person holding control over that other person, whether conducted within the country or between countries, for the purpose of exploitation or resulting in a person being exploited. 17. Discrimination is any distinction, harassment or exclusion that is direct or indirect based on human differentiation on the basis of religion, tribe, race, ethnic group, social status, economic status, gender, language, political beliefs that results in reduction, deviation or elimination of recognition, implementation or use of human rights and basic freedoms in life both individual and collective in the political, economic, legal, social, cultural fields and other aspects of life. 18. Maltreatment and/or treatment that degrades human dignity and worth is an action or attitude that is not in accordance with applicable moral, ethical, or legal norms encompassing various actions that harm others, whether physically, emotionally, or psychologically. 19. Exploitation is an action with or without the victim's consent that includes but is not limited to prostitution, forced labor or service, slavery or practices similar to slavery, oppression, extortion, utilization of physical, sexual, reproductive organs, or unlawfully removing or transplanting organs and/or body tissues or utilizing the labor or ability of a person by another party to obtain benefits both material and immaterial. 20. Sexual Exploitation is any form of utilization of sexual body organs or other body organs of the victim to obtain benefits, including but not limited to all prostitution and indecency activities. 21. Threat of violence is any unlawful act in the form of speech, writing, images, symbols, or body movements, whether with or without the use of means that causes fear or restricts a person's fundamental freedom. 22. Victim is a woman and child who experiences and/or suffers either directly or indirectly as a result of violence. 23. Rehabilitation is recovery from disruption to physical, psychological, and social conditions in order to be able to carry out their role again properly both in the family and in society. 24. Regional Technical Implementation Unit for Protection of Women and Children, abbreviated as UPTD-PPA is an Integrated Service Center established by the Regional Government to provide services to women and children victims of violence comprehensively including information services, assistance and legal aid, counseling services, medical services and safe houses through referral. 25. Task Force for Prevention and Handling of Violence Against Women and Children, hereinafter referred to as Task Force is a coordinating institution tasked with coordinating prevention and handling efforts of criminal acts of human trafficking in Pulang Pisau Regency. 26.

ELUCIDATION
OF
REGIONAL REGULATION OF PULANG PISAU
NUMBER 6 OF 2024
CONCERNING
THE IMPLEMENTATION OF PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN

I. GENERAL
Acts of violence against women and children constitute violations of human rights, therefore their dignity and honor need to be protected and their right to life guaranteed in accordance with their nature and disposition without discrimination.

In order to prevent and overcome violence against women and children in Pulang Pisau Regency so that they are protected from violence, threats of violence, torture or treatment that degrades human dignity and honor, it is necessary to provide protection for women and children in the form of regional regulations.

Thus far, laws and regulations governing the protection of women and children from acts of violence have not yet regulated protection efforts at the Regional level, therefore institutional support and regulations are needed that can guarantee its implementation.

The Regional Regulation regulates protection efforts for women and children, particularly in terms of prevention, services and empowerment of women and children from acts of violence in Pulang Pisau Regency.

Article 13
(1) The task force as referred to in Article 12 paragraph (3) letter a, shall consist of representatives from the Regional Government, law enforcement, community organizations, non-governmental organizations, professional organizations, and researchers/academics.
(2) The task force as referred to in Article 11 paragraph (3) letter a, is a coordinative institution tasked with coordinating the prevention and handling of acts of violence in various forms, exploitation, discrimination, mistreatment and/or treatment that demeans human dignity toward women and children.

Article 14
(1) The Committee as referred to in Article 12 paragraph (3) letter b, shall consist of representatives from the Regional Government, law enforcement, community organizations, non-governmental organizations, professional organizations, and researchers/academics.
(2) Further provisions regarding the duties and functions of the committee shall be stipulated by Regent's decree.

Article 17
(1) Regional governments establish partnerships with the business sector in the implementation of PPA.

   c. educational assistance for women and children victims of violence who have been withdrawn from their education; and
   d. fostering and enhancing economic independence of women victims of violence.
(3) Partnerships as referred to in paragraph (1) and paragraph (2) shall be set forth in the form of an agreement.

Article 20
Assistance is carried out by persons or institutions that have expertise to conduct counseling, therapy and advocacy for the strengthening and recovery of victims of violence and have cooperated with UPTD-PPA.

Article 8
(1) The obligations and responsibilities of the community as referred to in Article 6 letter b shall be implemented in the form of community participation. (2) The forms of community participation as referred to in paragraph (1), include:
a. preventing the occurrence of acts of violence in various forms, exploitation, discrimination, mistreatment and/or treatment that degrades the degree and dignity of humanity towards women and children;
b. providing information and/or reporting acts of violence in various forms, exploitation, discrimination, mistreatment and/or treatment that degrades the degree and dignity of humanity towards women and children to law enforcement or the authorized parties; and
c. participating in providing assistance and/or handling of victims of acts of violence in various forms, exploitation, discrimination, mistreatment and/or treatment that degrades the degree and dignity of humanity towards women and children.
(3) Forms of participation shall be implemented responsibly in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

CHAPTER I
GENERAL PROVISIONS
Article 1
In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:
1. Region is Pulang Pisau Regency. 2. Regional Government is the regional head as an element of regional government administration who leads the implementation of government affairs that are the authority of the autonomous region. 3. Regent is the Regent of Pulang Pisau. 4. Regional House of Representatives hereinafter abbreviated as DPRD is a regional people's representative institution that is positioned as an element of regional government administration. 5. Regional Apparatus is an auxiliary element of the Regional head and Regional House of Representatives in the administration of Government Affairs that are the authority of the Region. 6. Child is a person who has not reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including a child still in the womb. 7. Protection of Women and Children hereinafter abbreviated as PPA is a handling effort to protect and fulfill the rights of women and children from all forms of violence, discrimination, special protection, and other problems. 8. Violence is any unlawful act with or without the use of means against physical and psychological integrity that causes danger to life or body or results in the deprivation of a person's freedom. 9. Violence against women is any action based on gender differences that results in or may result in misery or suffering of women physically, sexually or psychologically, economic exploitation, social, including threats of certain actions, coercion or deprivation of freedom arbitrarily, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life. 10. Violence against children is any act against a child that results in misery or suffering physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically, economic exploitation, social, including neglect and maltreatment that threatens bodily integrity and degrades the dignity of the child. 11. Domestic violence is any act against a person especially women that results in misery or suffering physically, sexually, psychologically and or domestic neglect including threats to commit acts of coercion or deprivation of freedom unlawfully within the scope of the household. 12. Physical violence is any act that results in pain, injury, wounds or disability to a person's body, miscarriage, fainting and or causes death. 13. Sexual violence is any act in the form of sexual harassment, forced sexual intercourse, forced sexual intercourse in an unnatural or unwanted manner, forced sexual intercourse with others for commercial purposes and or certain purposes. 14. Economic violence is any act that deliberately neglects family members in the form of not providing a proper living care or maintenance. 15. Psychological violence is any act that results in fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and or severe psychological suffering to a person. 16. Human trafficking is the act of recruitment, transportation, harboring, sending, transfer, or receipt of a person by threat of violence, use of violence, abduction, confinement, forgery, fraud, abuse of power or position of vulnerability, debt bondage or giving payment or benefits, so as to obtain consent from the person holding control over that other person, whether conducted within the country or between countries, for the purpose of exploitation or resulting in a person being exploited. 17. Discrimination is any distinction, harassment or exclusion that is direct or indirect based on human differentiation on the basis of religion, tribe, race, ethnic group, social status, economic status, gender, language, political beliefs that results in reduction, deviation or elimination of recognition, implementation or use of human rights and basic freedoms in life both individual and collective in the political, economic, legal, social, cultural fields and other aspects of life. 18. Maltreatment and/or treatment that degrades human dignity and worth is an action or attitude that is not in accordance with applicable moral, ethical, or legal norms encompassing various actions that harm others, whether physically, emotionally, or psychologically. 19. Exploitation is an action with or without the victim's consent that includes but is not limited to prostitution, forced labor or service, slavery or practices similar to slavery, oppression, extortion, utilization of physical, sexual, reproductive organs, or unlawfully removing or transplanting organs and/or body tissues or utilizing the labor or ability of a person by another party to obtain benefits both material and immaterial. 20. Sexual Exploitation is any form of utilization of sexual body organs or other body organs of the victim to obtain benefits, including but not limited to all prostitution and indecency activities. 21. Threat of violence is any unlawful act in the form of speech, writing, images, symbols, or body movements, whether with or without the use of means that causes fear or restricts a person's fundamental freedom. 22. Victim is a woman and child who experiences and/or suffers either directly or indirectly as a result of violence. 23. Rehabilitation is recovery from disruption to physical, psychological, and social conditions in order to be able to carry out their role again properly both in the family and in society. 24.
